claims.text: LLMs using RAG can still produce unsupported or contradictory claims relative to retrieved contents.
RAGTruth comprises nearly 18,000 naturally generated responses from diverse LLMs using RAG with word-level and case-level manual hallucination annotations.
Finetuning a small LLM on RAGTruth achieves competitive hallucination detection performance compared to GPT-4 prompt-based approaches.

evidence.description: Despite the integration of RAG, LLMs may still present unsupported or contradictory claims to the retrieved contents.
RAGTruth comprises nearly 18,000 naturally generated responses from diverse LLMs using RAG, undergoing manual annotations at individual case and word levels.
Finetuning a relatively small LLM using RAGTruth achieves a competitive level of performance in hallucination detection compared to prompt-based approaches using GPT-4.

methodologies.name: RAGTruth Benchmark and Detection Finetuning
methodologies.description: A corpus of nearly 18,000 manual word- and case-level annotated RAG outputs used to benchmark hallucination detection methodologies and fine-tune smaller detection LLMs.

limitations.text: LLMs using RAG remain prone to presenting unsupported or contradictory claims relative to retrieved text.
